overview.about: World Ranger Day honours the park rangers who protect the world's natural and cultural heritage - often in dangerous conditions - and commemorates those killed or injured in the line of duty. It is organised each year by the International Ranger Federation.
overview.nextEvent: The next World Ranger Day is marked on 31 July with tributes, fundraising and events for rangers worldwide. It recognises their frontline role in protecting wildlife and wild places, and the risks they face.

@graph.name: World Ranger Day
@graph.description: World Ranger Day is observed on 31 July to remember rangers killed or injured while protecting natural and cultural heritage, and to recognise the people who work in parks, reserves and protected landscapes. The International Ranger Federation connects ranger organisations around the world, but the day is most meaningful when it points back to a specific protected place and the people who look after it. Rangers combine field knowledge, visitor safety, conservation work and community relationships; their work is not limited to wildlife patrols. Use the day to learn how a nearby park is managed, support a ranger organisation, or understand the pressures facing the habitats that visitors often take for granted.

exploreIntro: These places are selected for protected landscapes where ranger work is part of the conservation story: Australian parks and reefs, Kenyan wildlife reserves, and protected Alpine landscapes in Switzerland.
participationIntro: Use the day to recognise the people protecting parks and wildlife areas:

participationSteps.text: Share a ranger story, park update or conservation message from a trusted local or international source.
Thank or support ranger teams, park staff or conservation organisations where you have a real connection.
Use visits to parks and reserves responsibly: stay on marked routes, respect closures and do not disturb wildlife.
If there is a local event, use it to learn about ranger safety, protected areas and conservation work.
